 Haryana Plans Odour Control System at 24 Sewage Treatment Plants 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 The Haryana government has planned to install activated carbon-based odour-control systems at 24 Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) across the state to prevent foul smells and improve the quality of treated wastewater.   
 Key Points   
 Project Cost: The Haryana government has proposed an investment of approximately ₹38.6 crore .   
 Technology: The proposed systems will use activated carbon-based technology to control foul odours from sewage treatment plants.   
 Implementing Department: The initiative is being undertaken by the Public Health Engineering Department, Haryana.   
 Capacity: The department has identified 25 STPs with a combined treatment capacity of 230.5 MLD, currently treating 171.13 MLD of sewage daily.    
 Coverage: The proposed installations will cover 24 STPs i n locations including Ambala, Hisar, Hansi, Narnaund, Jind, Julana, Safidon, Fatehabad, Bhuna, Bhiwani, Siwani and Loharu, among others.   
 Objective: To eliminate foul odours from STPs, improve treated wastewater quality and promote its reuse, particularly for irrigation.    
 Related Government Initiatives:    
 Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0 (SBM 2.0): The Indian government shifted its focus towards solid waste, sludge and greywater management under this mission.   
 ODF Status: Following sustained efforts to achieve Open Defecation-Free (ODF) status, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) developed detailed criteria for cities to attain higher sanitation standards.   
 Sanitation Categories: In May 2020, MoHUA introduced detailed criteria for cities to achieve ODF+, ODF++ and Water+ statuses.   
 Read More: Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)

 MANAGE Hyderabad Recognised as Centre of Excellence-Skills in Agriculture Sector 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 The National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (MANAGE), Hyderabad, has been recognised as a Centre of Excellence-Skills (CoE-Skills) in the Agriculture Sector by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) , Government of India.    
 Key Points   
 Recognition Ceremony: The Certificate of Recognition was presented by Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE.   
 Validity: The recognition is valid for a period of three years.   
 About MANAGE: It is an autonomous organisation functioning under the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare .   
 Establishment: MANAGE was established in 1987.   
 Major Functions: The institute provides training, consultancy, research and policy support in agricultural extension.   
 Significance: The recognition will enable MANAGE to expand its role in agricultural skilling, strengthen institutional capacity and promote entrepreneurship in alignment with the Government of India's skill development mission.

 Cristiano Ronaldo Announces Retirement from International Football 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on 5 November 2026 , bringing an end to his 23-year career with the Portugal national team.    
 Key Points:   
 Ronaldo’s International Career   
 International debut: August 2003, against Kazakhstan.   
 International appearances: 234 matches, a men's world record.   
 International goals: 146 goals, the highest by any male footballer in international football.   
 Jersey number: Iconic No. 7 , popularly associated with his identity as CR7.   
 Ronaldo represented Portugal in six FIFA World Cup tournaments , from 2006 to 2026.   
 He became the first male footballer to score in six different FIFA World Cups .   
 Major Achievements with Portugal   
 UEFA Euro 2016: Captained Portugal to its first-ever European Championship title by defeating France 1–0 in the final.   
 UEFA Nations League 2019: Led Portugal to victory in the inaugural edition, defeating the Netherlands 1–0.   
 UEFA Nations League 2025: Captained Portugal to its second Nations League title, defeating Spain in the final.   
 FIFA World Cup: Scored in six consecutive editions of the tournament, an unprecedented achievement in men's football.   
 International scoring record: Finished his Portugal career with 146 goals in 234 appearances.   
 Ronaldo's Final International Records   
 234 appearances: Men's international appearance record.   
 146 goals: Men's international goal-scoring record.   
 41 goals: Highest number of goals in FIFA World Cup qualifying matches.   
 14 goals: Record number of goals in the UEFA European Championship finals.   
 30 appearances: Most matches played in UEFA European Championship tournaments.   
 Six World Cups: First male player to score in six different editions.   
 Five European Championships: First player to score in five different editions of the UEFA European Championship.   
 Continuation of Club Football   
 Ronaldo's retirement applies only to international football ; he will continue playing at club level.   
 Current club: Al-Nassr, Saudi Arabia.   
 At the time of his retirement announcement, he had scored approximately 985 career goals , including his international tally.

 QS Asia University Rankings 2027 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 The QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027 , released by global higher education analyst Quacquarelli Symonds (QS) on 3 November 2026 , placed IIT Delhi at 66th position , making it India's highest-ranked institution in Asia.    
 Key Points:   
 Major Highlights of QS Asia Rankings 2027   
 Publishing organisation: Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), a UK-based global higher education analytics and ranking organisation.   
 Total institutions: 1,722 universities.   
 Geographical coverage: 26 higher education systems across Asia.   
 Indian representation: 325 institutions, making India the second most represented higher education system after mainland China.   
 New entrants: 195 institutions entered the rankings for the first time globally.   
 Indian institutions in the top 200: 21, compared with 20 in the previous edition.   
 Performance trend in India:   
 71% of Indian universities recorded a decline in their rankings.   
 18% improved their positions.   
 11% remained stable.   
 Top Indian Institutions in QS Asia Rankings 2027   
 IIT Delhi: Retained its position as India's highest-ranked institution but fell seven places to now 66.   
 IISc Bengaluru: Ranked second among Indian institutions at 79th.   
 University of Delhi: Fell from 95th to 106th, moving outside the top 100.   
 Chandigarh University: Improved from 109th to 104th, achieving its best-ever position in the QS Asia Rankings.   
 Indian Universities Showing Improvement   
 Lovely Professional University: Improved from 187th to 154th.   
 Symbiosis International University: Improved from 200th to 175th.   
 Jamia Millia Islamia: Improved from 197th to 183rd.   
 Jawaharlal Nehru University: Improved from 130th to 128th.   
 IIT Hyderabad: Improved from 270th to 251st.   
 IIT (BHU) Varanasi: Improved from 237th to 219th.   
 IIT (ISM) Dhanbad: Climbed 51 places to 373rd.   
 Why Did Indian Universities Decline in the Rankings?   
 Intensifying regional competition: The entry of new institutions and improvement by established Asian universities increased competition.   
 Academic Reputation: This indicator carries a weightage of 30% . Scores declined for 76% of Indian universities.   
 Employer Reputation: It carries a weightage of 20% . Scores declined for 83% of Indian universities.   
 Internationalisation: Indian institutions faced weaknesses in international student recruitment and exchange indicators.   
 International student indicator declined for 85% of Indian universities.   
 Inbound exchange indicator declined for 91%.   
 Outbound exchange indicator declined for 89%.   
 Employer Reputation: Performance of IITs   
 IIT Bombay: Ranked 7th in Asia for Employer Reputation.   
 IIT Delhi: Ranked 10th in Asia for Employer Reputation.   
 These were the first Indian institutions to enter the top 10 in this indicator.   
 However, strong employer recognition remains concentrated among a limited number of Indian institutions.   
 About Quacquarelli Symonds (QS)   
 Full name: Quacquarelli Symonds.   
 Origin: United Kingdom.   
 Established: 1990.   
 Headquarters: London, United Kingdom.

 Rahul Dravid and Saina Nehwal Nominated to 2030 Commonwealth Games Organising Committee 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 The Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has nominated former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid and Olympic medallist Saina Nehwal as athlete representatives to the proposed Organising Committee (OC) for the 2030 Commonwealth Games (CWG) , which will be hosted by Ahmedabad, Gujarat .    
 Key Points:   
 Nominations to the Organising Committee   
 Rahul Dravid: Former Indian cricket captain and head coach of the Indian men's cricket team.   
 Saina Nehwal: Former Indian badminton player and 2012 London Olympics bronze medallist .   
 Purpose: Their nominations are intended to bring the experience and perspective of athletes into the planning and governance of the Games.   
 Committee Size: The proposed Organising Committee is expected to have 12–15 members .   
 Status: The nominations were confirmed by a Sports Ministry source on October 30, 2026. The formal composition of the committee was expected to be announced separately.   
 2030 Commonwealth Games:    
 Host City: Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India.   
 Edition: The 2030 edition will mark the centenary of the Commonwealth Games , first held in 1930.   
 Hosting Rights: India secured the hosting rights in November 2025 .   
 Proposed Sports: India is planning to include approximately 15–17 sporting disciplines .   
 Significance: The event will mark the return of the Commonwealth Games to India after the 2010 Delhi edition .   
 Proposed Sports Programme and Scale   
 Ahmedabad 2030: India is planning a programme of approximately 15–17 sports.   
 Glasgow 2026: The Games featured only 10 sporting disciplines , reflecting financial and organisational constraints.   
 Sports Omitted in Glasgow: Hockey, wrestling and cricket were among the prominent sports not included.   
 Expansion Objective: Ahmedabad's proposed programme is expected to offer a wider range of sporting disciplines than the Glasgow edition.   
 Commonwealth Games: Important Facts   
 First Edition: Held in 1930 at Hamilton, Canada .   
 Former Name: British Empire Games.   
 Frequency: Traditionally held once every four years.   
 Governing Body: Commonwealth Sport, formerly known as the Commonwealth Games Federation.   
 Participation: The event brings together athletes from countries and territories associated with the Commonwealth.   
 India's Performance: India hosted the Games in New Delhi in 2010 .   
 India's Best Performance: India finished second in the overall medal tally at the 2010 Delhi Commonwealth Games, winning 101 medals .
